reasons: Section 2.2 imposes a sole-and-exclusive supplier obligation on Customer for the full term with no product-category narrowing, no 12-month limit and no performance-based exit — this fails the fallback and sits in the rule's walk-away zone, so 'deviation' is the correct status.

The redline implements the preferred position with a targeted rewrite of the single offending sentence (non-exclusive appointment plus express right to procure from third parties); no exclusivity benefiting Customer is disturbed and Section 12.3 is left intact, consistent with the redline guidance.
The failed 'minimal edit' check (0.615 changed-character ratio) is advisory only and justified here: reversing an exclusivity grant necessarily requires rewriting the operative sentence.
The comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural with the required prefix, and correctly notes the conflict with Section 12.3 without lecturing.
Severity 'high' is appropriate for a full-term sole-supplier lock-in on our procurement freedom.
